author: Field notes of Tobias Grell, tinkerer
pages:
#Introduction

I have taken apart, with great care and considerable bleeding, nineteen Dwemer automatons. These notes describe what I found inside, and should be of use to anyone who plans to fight them, salvage them or, if they are as foolish as I am, repair them.

#The Spiders

The small eight-legged automatons are the most common. Inside each is a coiled spring of a metal I cannot identify, wound so tightly that releasing it carelessly will take your fingers off. Their legs end in blades. Their bodies house a little furnace of glowing stone that gives off a gentle warmth.

Strike at the joints where the legs meet the body. The plating there is thin, because the Dwemer valued movement over armour in these little guardians.

#The Spheres

The rolling automatons fold themselves into a ball and unfold into a warrior with a crossbow or blade on each arm. Their weakness is the moment of unfolding, when the plates part and the core is exposed. Strike then, or stand behind a pillar until they roll past.

Their cores glow brighter as they grow angry. I do not know whether this is a deliberate warning or a design flaw. I am grateful either way.

#The Centurions

I have seen only two of the great steam giants, and I took apart neither, because I did not survive the attempt so much as flee from it. They breathe scalding steam from vents in their chests and swing hammers the size of a cart.

If you must fight one, use the steam against it. The vents must open before it can breathe, and an arrow through an open vent seems to cause it real distress.

#On Salvage

Every automaton carries scraps of the golden-brown metal the Dwemer favoured. Smiths pay well for it. Bring a sack, and a friend to carry the sack, because the metal is heavy and the halls are long.

And for the love of all the Divines, do not wind the springs back up to see what happens. I have the scars to save you the trouble.
